english-grammar.q: The supervisor invited Ali and ____ to the classroom.
english-grammar.e: The pronoun is the object of “invited,” so the objective form “me” is required.

english-grammar.q: When I called, Mariam ____ dinner.
english-grammar.e: The past continuous shows the background action in progress when another past action occurred.

english-grammar.q: Which sentence uses the uncountable noun “advice” correctly?
english-grammar.e: “advice” is normally uncountable and is not used with a/an or a regular plural ending.

english-grammar.q: The study examined several ____ in detail.
english-grammar.e: “children” is the correct plural form of “child.”

english-grammar.q: The study examined many ____ in detail.
english-grammar.e: “women” is the correct plural form of “woman.”

english-grammar.q: The study examined a few ____ in detail.
english-grammar.e: “criteria” is the correct plural form of “criterion.”

english-grammar.q: The study examined two ____ in detail.
english-grammar.e: “analyses” is the correct plural form of “analysis.”

english-grammar.q: Choose the natural adjective order in Bilal's sentence about the classroom: She bought a ____ table.
english-grammar.e: Opinion normally precedes size, and material comes close to the noun.

english-grammar.q: The person to ____ Sara spoke was the director.
english-grammar.e: After the preposition “to,” formal grammar requires the objective relative pronoun “whom.”

english-grammar.q: The blue folders are ours; the green ones are ____.
english-grammar.e: A possessive pronoun stands alone, so “theirs” is required.

english-grammar.q: The train ____ at 6:30 tomorrow morning.
english-grammar.e: The present simple is used for fixed timetables and schedules.

english-grammar.q: The study examined three ____ in detail.
english-grammar.e: “phenomena” is the correct plural form of “phenomenon.”

english-grammar.q: The rules ____ by every employee.
english-grammar.e: A modal passive is modal + be + past participle.

english-grammar.q: How long ____ you ____ here?
english-grammar.e: A situation extending up to the present commonly takes the present perfect.

english-grammar.q: By next month, Ahmed ____ here for ten years.
english-grammar.e: The future perfect continuous emphasises duration up to a future point.

english-grammar.q: In Hamza's class at the classroom, only ____ students understood the exceptionally difficult rule.
english-grammar.e: “A few” means some and is used with a plural countable noun.

english-grammar.q: Of all the proposals reviewed by Bilal at the classroom, this one is the ____.
english-grammar.e: A comparison with all members of a group requires the superlative form.

english-grammar.q: In the profile displayed at the classroom, Ahmed is described as ____ hour-long interview.
english-grammar.e: “Hour” begins with a vowel sound because h is silent.

english-grammar.q: In British English, choose the sentence that treats “team” as individual members.
o: The team are divided in their opinions.
The team are divided in its opinion.
The team have divided in its opinions.
The team is divided in its opinions.
english-grammar.e: A collective noun may take a plural verb in British English when its members act separately.

english-grammar.q: For the course held at the classroom, Ahmed has read ____ book on the list.
english-grammar.e: “Every” is followed by a singular countable noun.

english-grammar.q: Ali ____ in Karachi for five years, but now lives elsewhere.
english-grammar.e: A finished period that no longer continues takes the past simple.

english-grammar.q: I ____ the door and ____ into the room.
english-grammar.e: Successive completed past actions are normally narrated in the past simple.

english-grammar.q: This is the researcher ____ discovered the error.
english-grammar.e: “Who” is the subject of the relative clause “who discovered the error.”

english-grammar.q: Neither of the answers explains ____ clearly.
english-grammar.e: “Neither” is grammatically singular, so the reflexive pronoun is “itself.”

english-grammar.q: I will call you as soon as the meeting ____.
english-grammar.e: Future time clauses after “as soon as” normally use the present simple, not “will.”

english-grammar.q: We ____ the director at noon tomorrow; the appointment is confirmed.
english-grammar.e: The present continuous can express a definite personal arrangement.

english-grammar.q: Look at those dark clouds; it ____ rain.
english-grammar.e: “Be going to” expresses a prediction based on present evidence.

english-grammar.q: During a trip organised by the classroom, Hamza visited ____ Indus River.
english-grammar.e: Names of rivers normally take the definite article “the.”

english-grammar.q: While Bilal waited near the classroom, the train arrived ____ late.
english-grammar.e: An adverb is required to modify the adjective/adverb “late.”

english-grammar.q: Someone has stolen the files. Choose the passive sentence.
english-grammar.e: The present perfect passive is have/has been + past participle.

english-grammar.q: People believe that the plan is effective. Choose the impersonal passive.
o: It has believed the plan effective.
The plan is believing to be effective.
It believes that the plan is effective.
It is believed that the plan is effective.
english-grammar.e: The impersonal passive uses “It + be + past participle + that-clause.”

english-grammar.q: Water ____ at 100°C at sea level.
english-grammar.e: The present simple states a general scientific fact.

english-grammar.q: I ____ what you mean.
english-grammar.e: Stative verbs such as “understand” are not normally used in the continuous for a present state.

english-grammar.q: This is the first time I ____ this software.
english-grammar.e: “This is the first time…” is normally followed by the present perfect.

countries-continents.q: On which continent is Georgia located?
countries-continents.e: GeoNames classifies Georgia in Asia.

countries-continents.q: On which continent is Colombia located?
countries-continents.e: GeoNames classifies Colombia in South America.

countries-continents.q: On which continent is Fiji located?
countries-continents.e: GeoNames classifies Fiji in Oceania.

countries-continents.q: On which continent is South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands located?
countries-continents.e: GeoNames classifies South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands in Antarctica.

environment.q: Which term means “Salt-tolerant coastal forest ecosystem”?
environment.e: Mangrove: Salt-tolerant coastal forest ecosystem. Protects shorelines and stores carbon

environment.q: Which term means “Increasing concentration of persistent substances at higher trophic levels”?
environment.e: Biomagnification: Increasing concentration of persistent substances at higher trophic levels. Classic example involves mercury

environment.q: Which term means “Reduction in stratospheric ozone”?
environment.e: Ozone depletion: Reduction in stratospheric ozone. Strongly linked to chlorofluorocarbons

environment.q: Which term means “Treaty controlling ozone-depleting substances”?
environment.e: Montreal Protocol: Treaty controlling ozone-depleting substances. Adopted in 1987

environment.q: Which term means “Stratospheric region with elevated ozone concentration”?
environment.e: Ozone layer: Stratospheric region with elevated ozone concentration. Absorbs much harmful ultraviolet radiation

environment.q: Which term means “Climate treaty aiming to strengthen global response to climate change”?
environment.e: Paris Agreement: Climate treaty aiming to strengthen global response to climate change. Adopted in 2015

environment.q: Which term means “Interaction benefiting one species without significant effect on the other”?
environment.e: Commensalism: Interaction benefiting one species without significant effect on the other. One species gains shelter or transport

environment.q: Which term means “Presence of people, ecosystems or assets in places that could be affected”?
environment.e: Exposure: Presence of people, ecosystems or assets in places that could be affected. A component of climate risk

environment.q: Which term means “Framework treaty for international climate cooperation”?
o: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
environment.e: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change: Framework treaty for international climate cooperation. Opened for signature in 1992

environment.q: Which term means “Establishment of forest on land not recently forested”?
environment.e: Afforestation: Establishment of forest on land not recently forested. Can increase carbon stocks when appropriately planned

environment.q: Which term means “Interaction benefiting a parasite while harming its host”?
environment.e: Parasitism: Interaction benefiting a parasite while harming its host. Usually does not immediately kill the host

environment.q: Which term means “Treaty setting emission targets for many developed countries”?
environment.e: Kyoto Protocol: Treaty setting emission targets for many developed countries. Adopted in 1997

environment.q: Which term means “Conversion or removal of forest cover”?
environment.e: Deforestation: Conversion or removal of forest cover. Reduces habitat and carbon storage

environment.q: Which term means “Interaction in which organisms seek the same limited resource”?
environment.e: Competition: Interaction in which organisms seek the same limited resource. Can occur within or between species

environment.q: Which term means “Treaty on conservation, sustainable use and benefit-sharing”?
environment.e: Convention on Biological Diversity: Treaty on conservation, sustainable use and benefit-sharing. Opened for signature in 1992

environment.q: Which term means “Land degradation in drylands”?
environment.e: Desertification: Land degradation in drylands. Driven by climatic variation and human activities

environment.q: Which term means “Interaction in which one organism kills and consumes another”?
environment.e: Predation: Interaction in which one organism kills and consumes another. Influences population dynamics

environment.q: Which term means “Interaction benefiting both participating species”?
environment.e: Mutualism: Interaction benefiting both participating species. Pollination is a common example

environment.q: Which term means “Capacity to absorb disturbance and retain essential functions”?
environment.e: Resilience: Capacity to absorb disturbance and retain essential functions. Applies to communities and ecosystems

environment.q: Which term means “Convention regulating international trade in endangered species”?
environment.e: CITES: Convention regulating international trade in endangered species. Uses appendices with different protection levels

environment.q: Which term means “Treaty protecting health and environment from mercury”?
environment.e: Minamata Convention: Treaty protecting health and environment from mercury. Adopted in 2013

environment.q: Which term means “Population growth slowing near carrying capacity”?
environment.e: Logistic growth: Population growth slowing near carrying capacity. Produces an S-shaped curve

environment.q: Which term means “Warming caused by atmospheric absorption and re-emission of infrared radiation”?
environment.e: Greenhouse effect: Warming caused by atmospheric absorption and re-emission of infrared radiation. Natural process intensified by added greenhouse gases

environment.q: Which term means “Adjustment to actual or expected climate effects”?
environment.e: Adaptation: Adjustment to actual or expected climate effects. Can reduce harm or exploit beneficial opportunities

environment.q: Which term means “Treaty for conservation and wise use of wetlands”?
environment.e: Ramsar Convention: Treaty for conservation and wise use of wetlands. Adopted in 1971

environment.q: Which term means “Land saturated or flooded long enough to support adapted ecosystems”?
environment.e: Wetland: Land saturated or flooded long enough to support adapted ecosystems. Provides flood regulation and habitat

environment.q: Which term means “Gas that absorbs and emits infrared radiation”?
environment.e: Greenhouse gas: Gas that absorbs and emits infrared radiation. Examples include carbon dioxide and methane

environment.q: Which term means “Potential occurrence of an event causing harm”?
environment.e: Hazard: Potential occurrence of an event causing harm. Examples include floods and heatwaves

environment.q: Which term means “Accumulation of salts in soil”?
environment.e: Salinization: Accumulation of salts in soil. Often associated with irrigation and poor drainage

environment.q: Which term means “Long-term statistical pattern of weather”?
environment.e: Climate: Long-term statistical pattern of weather. Usually assessed over decades

environment.q: Which term means “Propensity to be adversely affected”?
environment.e: Vulnerability: Propensity to be adversely affected. Depends on exposure, sensitivity and adaptive capacity

environment.q: Which term means “Removal of topsoil by water, wind or other agents”?
o: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
environment.e: Soil erosion: Removal of topsoil by water, wind or other agents. Can reduce agricultural productivity

environment.q: Which term means “Short-term atmospheric conditions”?
environment.e: Weather: Short-term atmospheric conditions. Includes temperature, precipitation and wind

environment.q: Which term means “Long-term rise in global average surface temperature”?
environment.e: Global warming: Long-term rise in global average surface temperature. A major component of current climate change

environment.q: Which term means “Long-lived greenhouse gas and ozone-depleting substance”?
environment.e: Nitrous oxide: Long-lived greenhouse gas and ozone-depleting substance. Major human source is agricultural soil management

environment.q: Which term means “Human intervention to reduce emissions or enhance sinks”?
environment.e: Mitigation: Human intervention to reduce emissions or enhance sinks. Renewable energy and efficiency are examples

environment.q: Which term means “Long-term change in climate state or variability”?
environment.e: Climate change: Long-term change in climate state or variability. Human influence is the dominant cause of recent warming

environment.q: Which term means “Study of interactions among organisms and their environment”?
environment.e: Ecology: Study of interactions among organisms and their environment. Foundation of ecosystem analysis

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Community.
o: High risk of extinction in the wild
Charismatic species used to mobilize conservation support
Populations of different species living together
Species with a disproportionately large ecological effect
environment.e: Community: Populations of different species living together. Species interact through competition, predation and mutualism

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Population.
o: Increasing concentration of persistent substances at higher trophic levels
Individuals of the same species in a defined area
environment.e: Population: Individuals of the same species in a defined area. Population size changes through births, deaths and migration

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Ecological niche.
o: Functional role and environmental requirements of a species
Nutrient enrichment causing excessive plant or algal growth
Processing waste into materials or products
environment.e: Ecological niche: Functional role and environmental requirements of a species. Includes resource use and interactions

environment.q: Which term means “Community of organisms interacting with the physical environment”?
environment.e: Ecosystem: Community of organisms interacting with the physical environment. Includes biotic and abiotic components

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Habitat.
o: Natural place where an organism lives
Long-lived greenhouse gas and ozone-depleting substance
Non-native species causing ecological or economic harm
System aiming to reduce waste and keep materials in use
environment.e: Habitat: Natural place where an organism lives. Provides resources and conditions for survival

environment.q: Which term means “Large ecological region defined by climate and dominant vegetation”?
environment.e: Biome: Large ecological region defined by climate and dominant vegetation. Examples include tundra and tropical rainforest

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Ecosystem diversity.
o: Population growth at a constant proportional rate
Variety of ecosystems in a region
Interaction benefiting one species without significant effect on the other
environment.e: Ecosystem diversity: Variety of ecosystems in a region. Includes forests, wetlands and grasslands

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Species diversity.
o: Variety and relative abundance of species
Conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into biologically usable forms
Movement and transformation of nitrogen in ecosystems
environment.e: Species diversity: Variety and relative abundance of species. Includes richness and evenness

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Genetic diversity.
o: Measure of biologically productive area needed to support consumption and absorb wastes
Variation of genes within a species
Nutrient enrichment causing excessive plant or algal growth
Species used to assess environmental conditions
environment.e: Genetic diversity: Variation of genes within a species. Helps populations adapt to change

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Biodiversity.
o: Variety of life at genetic, species and ecosystem levels
Interaction in which organisms seek the same limited resource
Conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into biologically usable forms
environment.e: Biodiversity: Variety of life at genetic, species and ecosystem levels. Supports resilience and ecosystem services

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Native species.
o: Study of interactions among organisms and their environment
Process evaluating likely environmental effects before approval
Species whose conservation protects many co-occurring species
Species occurring naturally in an area
environment.e: Native species: Species occurring naturally in an area. Not introduced by human activity

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Endemic species.
o: Species with a disproportionately large ecological effect
Conversion or removal of forest cover
Species naturally restricted to a particular area
Land saturated or flooded long enough to support adapted ecosystems
environment.e: Endemic species: Species naturally restricted to a particular area. Often vulnerable to habitat loss

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Eutrophication.
o: Long-term change in climate state or variability
Finite resource not replenished on human timescales
Defined marine area managed for conservation
Nutrient enrichment causing excessive plant or algal growth
environment.e: Eutrophication: Nutrient enrichment causing excessive plant or algal growth. Can lead to oxygen depletion

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Nitrogen fixation.
o: Extremely high risk of extinction in the wild
Loss of symbiotic algae or pigments from stressed corals
Conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into biologically usable forms
environment.e: Nitrogen fixation: Conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into biologically usable forms. Performed by certain microbes and lightning

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Nitrogen cycle.
o: Movement and transformation of nitrogen in ecosystems
Conversion of light energy into chemical energy by producers
High risk of extinction in the wild
Mixture of airborne solid particles and liquid droplets
environment.e: Nitrogen cycle: Movement and transformation of nitrogen in ecosystems. Includes fixation and denitrification

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Carbon cycle.
o: Movement of carbon among atmosphere, oceans, organisms and rocks
Interaction in which one organism kills and consumes another
Community of organisms interacting with the physical environment
environment.e: Carbon cycle: Movement of carbon among atmosphere, oceans, organisms and rocks. Affected by fossil-fuel combustion

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Phosphorus cycle.
o: Variety of life at genetic, species and ecosystem levels
Species naturally restricted to a particular area
Species whose conservation protects many co-occurring species
Movement of phosphorus through rocks, soil, water and organisms
environment.e: Phosphorus cycle: Movement of phosphorus through rocks, soil, water and organisms. Has no major gaseous phase

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Water cycle.
o: Movement of water through evaporation, condensation and precipitation
Processing waste into materials or products
Long-term rise in global average surface temperature
Long-lived greenhouse gas from natural and human sources
environment.e: Water cycle: Movement of water through evaporation, condensation and precipitation. Also called hydrological cycle

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Detritivore.
o: Harmful change in water temperature from human activity
Animal that consumes dead organic matter
Movement of phosphorus through rocks, soil, water and organisms
Linear transfer of energy through feeding relationships
environment.e: Detritivore: Animal that consumes dead organic matter. Examples include many earthworms

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Decomposer.
o: Organism breaking down dead organic material
Process evaluating likely environmental effects before approval
Conversion of light energy into chemical energy by producers
environment.e: Decomposer: Organism breaking down dead organic material. Returns nutrients to ecosystems

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Cellular respiration.
o: Acidic deposition formed mainly from sulfur and nitrogen oxides
Release of energy from organic molecules
Population growth slowing near carrying capacity
Species whose conservation protects many co-occurring species
environment.e: Cellular respiration: Release of energy from organic molecules. Produces carbon dioxide and water in aerobic respiration

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Photosynthesis.
o: Animal that consumes dead organic matter
Conversion of light energy into chemical energy by producers
Nutrient enrichment causing excessive plant or algal growth
Potent greenhouse gas with shorter atmospheric lifetime than carbon dioxide
environment.e: Photosynthesis: Conversion of light energy into chemical energy by producers. Consumes carbon dioxide and releases oxygen

environment.q: What is the best definition of Air pollution?
o: Variety of ecosystems in a region
Contamination of the atmosphere by harmful substances
Treaty setting emission targets for many developed countries
environment.e: Air pollution: Contamination of the atmosphere by harmful substances. Includes particulate matter and ozone

environment.q: What is the best definition of Particulate matter?
o: Mixture of airborne solid particles and liquid droplets
Defined marine area managed for conservation
Assessment of environmental impacts across a product's life cycle
environment.e: Particulate matter: Mixture of airborne solid particles and liquid droplets. PM2.5 penetrates deeply into lungs

environment.q: What is the best definition of Acid rain?
o: Treaty protecting health and environment from mercury
Capacity to absorb disturbance and retain essential functions
Acidic deposition formed mainly from sulfur and nitrogen oxides
environment.e: Acid rain: Acidic deposition formed mainly from sulfur and nitrogen oxides. Can acidify soils and waters

environment.q: What is the best definition of Smog?
o: Process evaluating likely environmental effects before approval
Decline in ocean pH caused mainly by absorbed carbon dioxide
Air pollution mixture reducing visibility and harming health
Nutrient enrichment causing excessive plant or algal growth
environment.e: Smog: Air pollution mixture reducing visibility and harming health. Photochemical smog involves ground-level ozone

environment.q: What is the best definition of Ecological footprint?
o: Measure of biologically productive area needed to support consumption and absorb wastes
Variety and relative abundance of species
Interaction benefiting one species without significant effect on the other
environment.e: Ecological footprint: Measure of biologically productive area needed to support consumption and absorb wastes. Compared with biocapacity

environment.q: What is the best definition of Reforestation?
o: Re-establishment of forest on recently forested land
Development meeting present needs without compromising future generations
Nutrient enrichment causing excessive plant or algal growth
environment.e: Reforestation: Re-establishment of forest on recently forested land. Supports restoration and carbon sequestration

environment.q: What is the best definition of Life-cycle assessment?
o: Large ecological region defined by climate and dominant vegetation
Assessment of environmental impacts across a product's life cycle
environment.e: Life-cycle assessment: Assessment of environmental impacts across a product's life cycle. Covers raw materials through disposal

environment.q: What is the best definition of Afforestation?
o: Variation of genes within a species
Large ecological region defined by climate and dominant vegetation
Establishment of forest on land not recently forested
environment.e: Afforestation: Establishment of forest on land not recently forested. Can increase carbon stocks when appropriately planned

environment.q: What is the best definition of Environmental impact assessment?
o: Establishment of forest on land not recently forested
Process evaluating likely environmental effects before approval
Organism breaking down dead organic material
Populations of different species living together
environment.e: Environmental impact assessment: Process evaluating likely environmental effects before approval. Supports informed decision-making

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Commensalism.
o: Movement of phosphorus through rocks, soil, water and organisms
Interaction benefiting one species without significant effect on the other
Human intervention to reduce emissions or enhance sinks
Nutrient enrichment causing excessive plant or algal growth
environment.e: Commensalism: Interaction benefiting one species without significant effect on the other. One species gains shelter or transport

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Parasitism.
o: Populations of different species living together
Species occurring naturally in an area
Interaction benefiting a parasite while harming its host
Large ecological region defined by climate and dominant vegetation
environment.e: Parasitism: Interaction benefiting a parasite while harming its host. Usually does not immediately kill the host

environment.q: What is the best definition of Water pollution?
o: Capacity to absorb disturbance and retain essential functions
environment.e: Water pollution: Contamination degrading water quality. Sources include sewage, industry and agriculture

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Competition.
o: Succession where soil remains after disturbance
Interaction in which organisms seek the same limited resource
Individuals of the same species in a defined area
environment.e: Competition: Interaction in which organisms seek the same limited resource. Can occur within or between species

environment.q: What is the best definition of CITES?
o: Variation of genes within a species
Geographically defined area managed for long-term conservation
Loss of symbiotic algae or pigments from stressed corals
Convention regulating international trade in endangered species
environment.e: CITES: Convention regulating international trade in endangered species. Uses appendices with different protection levels

environment.q: What is the best definition of Thermal pollution?
o: Contamination of the atmosphere by harmful substances
Harmful change in water temperature from human activity
Species used to assess environmental conditions
environment.e: Thermal pollution: Harmful change in water temperature from human activity. Can lower dissolved oxygen

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Mutualism.
o: Directional change in community composition over time
Populations of different species living together
Human intervention to reduce emissions or enhance sinks
environment.e: Mutualism: Interaction benefiting both participating species. Pollination is a common example

environment.q: What is the best definition of Convention on Biological Diversity?
o: Succession where soil remains after disturbance
Treaty on conservation, sustainable use and benefit-sharing
environment.e: Convention on Biological Diversity: Treaty on conservation, sustainable use and benefit-sharing. Opened for signature in 1992

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Greenhouse effect.
o: Warming caused by atmospheric absorption and re-emission of infrared radiation
High risk of extinction in the wild
Large ecological region defined by climate and dominant vegetation
environment.e: Greenhouse effect: Warming caused by atmospheric absorption and re-emission of infrared radiation. Natural process intensified by added greenhouse gases

environment.q: What is the best definition of Basel Convention?
o: High risk of extinction in the wild
Acidic deposition formed mainly from sulfur and nitrogen oxides
Treaty controlling transboundary movements of hazardous wastes
environment.e: Basel Convention: Treaty controlling transboundary movements of hazardous wastes. Adopted in 1989

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Greenhouse gas.
o: Gas that absorbs and emits infrared radiation
Increasing concentration of persistent substances at higher trophic levels
Resource replenished naturally on human timescales
Process evaluating likely environmental effects before approval
environment.e: Greenhouse gas: Gas that absorbs and emits infrared radiation. Examples include carbon dioxide and methane

environment.q: What is the best definition of Ramsar Convention?
o: Defined marine area managed for conservation
Treaty controlling transboundary movements of hazardous wastes
Treaty for conservation and wise use of wetlands
Build-up of a substance within an organism over time
environment.e: Ramsar Convention: Treaty for conservation and wise use of wetlands. Adopted in 1971

environment.q: What is the best definition of Primary consumer?
o: Treaty setting emission targets for many developed countries
Harmful change in water temperature from human activity
environment.e: Primary consumer: Organism that feeds on producers. Commonly an herbivore

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Climate.
o: Capacity to absorb disturbance and retain essential functions
Framework treaty for international climate cooperation
Treaty for conservation and wise use of wetlands
environment.e: Climate: Long-term statistical pattern of weather. Usually assessed over decades

environment.q: What is the best definition of Flagship species?
o: Population growth at a constant proportional rate
Charismatic species used to mobilize conservation support
Movement of water through evaporation, condensation and precipitation
Convention regulating international trade in endangered species
environment.e: Flagship species: Charismatic species used to mobilize conservation support. Often used in public campaigns

environment.q: Select the accurate description of Weather.
o: Interaction benefiting a parasite while harming its host
Species occurring naturally in an area
Large ecological region defined by climate and dominant vegetation
environment.e: Weather: Short-term atmospheric conditions. Includes temperature, precipitation and wind

environment.q: What is the best definition of Umbrella species?
o: Species whose conservation protects many co-occurring species
Conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into biologically usable forms
Measure of biologically productive area needed to support consumption and absorb wastes
Very high risk of extinction in the wild
environment.e: Umbrella species: Species whose conservation protects many co-occurring species. Requires large or diverse habitat

environment.q: What is the best definition of Deforestation?
o: Conversion or removal of forest cover
Extremely high risk of extinction in the wild
environment.e: Deforestation: Conversion or removal of forest cover. Reduces habitat and carbon storage

environment.q: What is the best definition of Indicator species?
o: Species used to assess environmental conditions
Waste posing substantial risk because of toxic, reactive or other properties
Natural place where an organism lives
environment.e: Indicator species: Species used to assess environmental conditions. Lichens may indicate air quality

environment.q: What is the best definition of Desertification?
o: Development meeting present needs without compromising future generations
Species used to assess environmental conditions
environment.e: Desertification: Land degradation in drylands. Driven by climatic variation and human activities

environment.q: What is the best definition of Food chain?
o: Long-lived greenhouse gas from natural and human sources
Waste posing substantial risk because of toxic, reactive or other properties
Linear transfer of energy through feeding relationships
environment.e: Food chain: Linear transfer of energy through feeding relationships. Begins with producers in most ecosystems

economics.q: Which economic term means “Cost or benefit imposed on a third party”?
economics.e: Externality: Cost or benefit imposed on a third party. Can be positive or negative

economics.q: Which economic term means “Curve showing maximum feasible output combinations”?
economics.e: Production possibility frontier: Curve showing maximum feasible output combinations. Points inside indicate underused resources

economics.q: Which economic term means “Difference between market price and minimum acceptable price”?
economics.e: Producer surplus: Difference between market price and minimum acceptable price. Measures seller benefit

economics.q: Which economic term means “Quantity consumers are willing and able to buy at different prices”?
economics.e: Demand: Quantity consumers are willing and able to buy at different prices. Usually slopes downward, other things equal

economics.q: Which economic term means “Resource that is rival but difficult to exclude users from”?
economics.e: Common-pool resource: Resource that is rival but difficult to exclude users from. Can face overuse

economics.q: Which economic term means “Limited resources relative to unlimited wants”?
economics.e: Scarcity: Limited resources relative to unlimited wants. Makes choices and trade-offs necessary

economics.q: Which economic term means “Good that is non-rival and non-excludable”?
economics.e: Public good: Good that is non-rival and non-excludable. National defence is a common example

economics.q: Which economic term means “Sustained decrease in the general price level”?
economics.e: Deflation: Sustained decrease in the general price level. Can increase real burden of debt

economics.q: Which economic term means “Value of the next best alternative forgone”?
economics.e: Opportunity cost: Value of the next best alternative forgone. Relevant cost of a choice

economics.q: Which economic term means “Responsiveness of demand to income change”?
economics.e: Income elasticity of demand: Responsiveness of demand to income change. Can distinguish normal and inferior goods

economics.q: Which economic term means “Decline in the rate of inflation”?
economics.e: Disinflation: Decline in the rate of inflation. Prices may still be rising more slowly

economics.q: Which economic term means “Responsiveness of quantity demanded to a price change”?
economics.e: Price elasticity of demand: Responsiveness of quantity demanded to a price change. Elasticity greater than one is elastic

economics.q: Which economic term means “Difference between willingness to pay and actual price”?
economics.e: Consumer surplus: Difference between willingness to pay and actual price. Measures buyer benefit

economics.q: Which economic term means “Quantity producers are willing and able to sell at different prices”?
economics.e: Supply: Quantity producers are willing and able to sell at different prices. Usually slopes upward, other things equal

economics.q: Which economic term means “Responsiveness of demand for one good to another good's price”?
economics.e: Cross-price elasticity: Responsiveness of demand for one good to another good's price. Positive for substitutes and negative for complements

economics.q: Which economic term means “Price and quantity where demand equals supply”?
economics.e: Market equilibrium: Price and quantity where demand equals supply. No tendency for price to change absent shocks

economics.q: Which economic term means “Minimum reserves banks must hold against deposits”?
economics.e: Reserve requirement: Minimum reserves banks must hold against deposits. Affects money creation

economics.q: Which economic term means “Central-bank purchases or sales of securities”?
economics.e: Open market operations: Central-bank purchases or sales of securities. Used to manage liquidity and interest rates

economics.q: Which economic term means “Market with many firms, homogeneous products and free entry”?
economics.e: Perfect competition: Market with many firms, homogeneous products and free entry. Individual firms are price takers

economics.q: Which economic term means “Market dominated by a small number of firms”?
economics.e: Oligopoly: Market dominated by a small number of firms. Strategic interdependence is important

economics.q: Which economic term means “Market with many firms selling differentiated products”?
economics.e: Monopolistic competition: Market with many firms selling differentiated products. Firms have some pricing power

economics.q: Which economic term means “Market with a single dominant seller and high barriers to entry”?
economics.e: Monopoly: Market with a single dominant seller and high barriers to entry. Possesses market power

economics.q: Which economic term means “Market value of final goods and services produced within a country”?
economics.e: Gross domestic product: Market value of final goods and services produced within a country. Measures domestic production

economics.q: Which economic term means “Income earned by a country's residents including net income from abroad”?
economics.e: Gross national income: Income earned by a country's residents including net income from abroad. Focuses on residents rather than location of production

economics.q: Which economic term means “Unemployment from mismatch of skills or locations”?
economics.e: Structural unemployment: Unemployment from mismatch of skills or locations. Can persist despite vacancies

economics.q: Which economic term means “GDP measured at current prices”?
economics.e: Nominal GDP: GDP measured at current prices. Affected by price changes

economics.q: Which economic term means “Short-term unemployment during job search and transitions”?
economics.e: Frictional unemployment: Short-term unemployment during job search and transitions. Exists even in healthy labour markets

economics.q: Which economic term means “GDP adjusted for changes in the price level”?
economics.e: Real GDP: GDP adjusted for changes in the price level. Used to measure output growth

economics.q: Which economic term means “Share of the labour force without work but seeking and available for work”?
economics.e: Unemployment rate: Share of the labour force without work but seeking and available for work. Excludes people outside the labour force

economics.q: Which economic term means “Broad price index derived from nominal and real GDP”?
economics.e: GDP deflator: Broad price index derived from nominal and real GDP. Covers domestically produced final output

economics.q: Which economic term means “Index tracking prices of a representative consumer basket”?
economics.e: Consumer price index: Index tracking prices of a representative consumer basket. Common measure of cost-of-living changes

economics.q: Which economic term means “Benchmark rate set or targeted by a central bank”?
economics.e: Policy interest rate: Benchmark rate set or targeted by a central bank. Influences borrowing conditions

economics.q: Which economic term means “Central-bank management of money and interest-rate conditions”?
economics.e: Monetary policy: Central-bank management of money and interest-rate conditions. Aims commonly include price stability

economics.q: Which economic term means “Government use of spending and taxation to influence the economy”?
economics.e: Fiscal policy: Government use of spending and taxation to influence the economy. Can be expansionary or contractionary

economics.q: Which economic term means “Unemployment caused by economic downturns”?
economics.e: Cyclical unemployment: Unemployment caused by economic downturns. Rises during recessions

economics.q: Which field of economics best fits Comparative advantage?
economics.e: Comparative advantage: Ability to produce at lower opportunity cost. Explains gains from specialization

economics.q: Which field of economics best fits Tariff?
economics.e: Tariff: Tax imposed on imported goods. Raises domestic price of imports

economics.q: Which field of economics best fits Poverty line?
economics.e: Poverty line: Income or consumption threshold used to identify poverty. Can be national or international

economics.q: Which field of economics best fits Foreign direct investment?
economics.e: Foreign direct investment: Cross-border investment involving lasting control or influence. Includes greenfield investment and acquisitions

economics.q: Which field of economics best fits Subsidy?
economics.e: Subsidy: Government payment or support lowering costs or prices. Can correct externalities or distort markets

economics.q: Which field of economics best fits Cyclical unemployment?
economics.e: Cyclical unemployment: Unemployment caused by economic downturns. Rises during recessions

economics.q: Which field of economics best fits Fiscal policy?
economics.e: Fiscal policy: Government use of spending and taxation to influence the economy. Can be expansionary or contractionary

economics.q: Which field of economics best fits Opportunity cost?
economics.e: Opportunity cost: Value of the next best alternative forgone. Relevant cost of a choice

economics.q: Which field of economics best fits Trade deficit?
economics.e: Trade deficit: Imports of goods and services exceed exports. A component of the current account

economics.q: Which field of economics best fits Consumer price index?
economics.e: Consumer price index: Index tracking prices of a representative consumer basket. Common measure of cost-of-living changes

economics.q: Which field of economics best fits Multiplier?
economics.e: Multiplier: Ratio of total income change to an initial autonomous spending change. Depends partly on marginal propensity to consume

economics.q: Which field of economics best fits Reserve requirement?
economics.e: Reserve requirement: Minimum reserves banks must hold against deposits. Affects money creation
